title: the harbor master proves its map wears the one status label operator_inbox's reader derives
intention: The harbor map's half of 'a ticket has ONE status' (ticket 3feb201c84ea) is measured today only from cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_one_status_everywhere.py, which imports the harbor master's device and register (:81,:82), a RULE 1 breach. The harbor master's own proof holds it here: over the same fixture and over the live world the open map's rows wear operator_inbox.read_tickets' label, its status groups are the inbox header's counts in its order, a prose history standing is a FINDING line, and a crossing patch reloads the ticket.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: encapsulation_holds names cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_one_status_everywhere.py:81,82 and cairn/tools/operator_inbox/probes/one_status_everywhere.py:58. RULE 1: a ticket's proofs measure only that component, so the map's teeth berth with the harbor master before operator_inbox drops its copies.
traces_to: CLAUDE.md RULE 1; outline 2.3.7.1 (a device's public interface is the bus plus any tool it publishes); outline 17.13.1.
how: New proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/proofs/test_the_map_wears_the_one_label.py builds the seven-ticket fixture (THINKME, TICKETME:waiting, PROVEME:waiting, WATCHME(fx):waiting, WATCHME(fx), PROVED, a prose cursor; fx_widget's history standing is prose), renders register(cairn_root=, tickets_dir=) through _filter_fleet(open) and _render_fleet_map, and compares the printed rows and group headers with read_tickets and format_summary. The prose-standing and crossing-patch teeth move here verbatim; a live tooth compares `show map open` with the live reader. No code change.
